fig1_claim_protein_divergence: Fig. 1 | Protein divergence within S. cerevisiae, within Saccharomyces and within mammals on one axis. Each point is a pair; the y axis is 100 minus protein identity (log scale, inverted; identity on the right). Within S. cerevisiae (n = 1,011 isolates): the mean over S288C reference ORFs of each isolate's protein identity to S288C, from Peter 2018's reference-inferred alleles, with every gap column of a frameshifted or indel-bearing ORF charged (06_isolate_protein_identity.py); the per-isolate MEDIAN over ORFs, which frameshifted ORFs do not pull down, gives a median divergence of 0.28%. Every other column: AAI, the mean percent identity over reciprocal best mmseqs2 hits of one-protein-per-gene proteomes (03_mmseqs_rbh.py); n pairs per column Within Saccharomyces 3, Within mammals 28, Mammal vs chicken 8, Within Saccharomycotina 75, Within bacteria 45, Saccharomycotina vs bacteria 130. Open diamonds: AAI restricted to Eukaryota-level eggNOG OGs that are single copy in both members, the proxy for Peris et al. 2023's BUSCO AAI. Point face and edge colors are the taxonomic groups of the two members. Gray band: one human genome differs from GRCh38 at 10,000 to 12,000 peptide-altering sites (1000 Genomes Project 2015, doi:10.1038/nature15393; literature value, not computed here), divided by this study's 11.7 million-residue human per-gene proteome.
fig2_cladogram_heatmaps: Fig. 2 | The organisms torchcell serves or targets on three similarity axes, ordered by the NCBI taxonomy. Left: NCBI taxonomy cladogram (topology only; ete3 NCBITaxa, 05_trees.py) of the 34 reference organisms; the strip is the plan's first group per organism. Heatmaps, rows and columns in cladogram order: AAI (mean percent identity over reciprocal best hits, 03_mmseqs_rbh.py), ortholog Jaccard (RBH count over the union of the two per-gene proteomes) and EC-4 Jaccard (complete EC numbers from one eggNOG-mapper 2 run, eggNOG 5.0.2, 04_emapper.py). Gray: no proteome (A. limacinum has no annotated assembly at NCBI) or the diagonal.
fig3_taxonomy_vs_aai_nj: Fig. 3 | NCBI taxonomy and AAI agree on the large groups. Left: NCBI taxonomy cladogram (topology only) over the 33 organisms with a proteome. Right: neighbor-joining tree (Biopython) on d = -ln(AAI/100), rooted with the bacteria as outgroup, drawn as topology with children rotated to follow the left tree. Lines join the same organism and are colored by its taxonomic group (05_trees.py).
fig4_isolate_tree: Fig. 4 | The 1,011 S. cerevisiae isolates. rapidnj neighbor-joining tree on Peter et al. 2018's SNP distance matrix (percent non-identical bases, heterozygous differences half-weighted), midpoint rooted (05_trees.py). Strip: clade from Peter's Supplementary Table 1 (962 of 1,011 isolates carry one; the 17 largest clades in color, the remaining 12 in one color; Wine/European subclades merged). Arrow: ADT, the isolate with the lowest mean per-ORF nucleotide divergence from S288C in 018 (0.0005%); S288C itself is not in Peter's matrix.
fig5_ortholog_fraction_vs_aai: Fig. 5 | Shared orthologs fall with AAI. Each point is one of the 528 pairs of the 33 proteomes: AAI (mean RBH percent identity) against the ortholog fraction, reciprocal best hits over the smaller per-gene proteome (03_mmseqs_rbh.py). Face and edge colors are the taxonomic groups of the two members.
